Data.title: Big News from Wall Street About This Altcoin: It Will Be Used on the New York Stock Exchange’s New Platform
Data.body: Avalanche is poised to play a significant role in Wall Street’s blockchain initiative. Ava Labs announced today that its tokenized securities platform, developed in conjunction with the New York Stock Exchange, will utilize Avalanche as its clearing infrastructure. Avalanche will provide the platform’s clearing house with the core ledger technology for recording and settling transactions. Following the necessary regulatory approvals, the system aims to offer trading and clearing services 24/7. Dennis Lee, Head of Digital Issuance at the NYSE, listed speed, reliability, predictable costs, and control over who can participate in the system as reasons for choosing Avalanche. Lee stated that Avalanche meets these needs. Related News: A Very Controversial Statement from the Zilliqa Team About Another Altcoin: “If Satoshi Were Alive Today, He’d Be Working Here” Emin Gün Sirer, founder of Ava Labs, stated that the infrastructure would be designed to meet the need for seamless and simultaneous exchanges. Sirer emphasized the importance of organizations being able to meet their regulatory and operational obligations. The platform also plans to support shares issued on different blockchain networks. Avalanche’s role will be to provide the recording and clearing infrastructure for these transactions. Today’s announcement officially confirms Avalanche’s role, while the licensing process for the platform to become operational is ongoing. Following this development, AVAX price experienced a noticeable increase. The chart shows the increase in AVAX price. *This is not investment advice. It goes after operators, not punters. To enforce it, the ACMA gets internet providers to block offending sites, and by mid-2026 more than 1,700 had copped a block. Coin volatility: a bonus pegged in BTC shrinks in dollar terms if the price dips mid-wager. 👉 Rule of thumb: if you play often, wager-free cashback or rakeback usually beats a giant match you’ll never clear. All three nail the basics that the best crypto casinos should always get right. You get a licence you can verify, clear withdrawal rules and payouts that actually land on time. So start small. Test a withdrawal early. And keep it fun. FAQ Can I play crypto casino games on my phone in Australia? Yes, easily. Most crypto sites run smoothly in your phone’s browser on iOS or Android, and plenty let you pin a shortcut to the home screen. Proper apps are rare, though, because app stores restrict real-money gambling apps from offshore operators. What is the minimum deposit at a crypto casino? Data.title: Coinbase Secures OCC Approval for National Trust Charter
Data.body: Coinbase secures OCC unconditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to operate under a federal national trust bank charter, the company announced Monday. The decision marks a significant regulatory milestone for the largest U.S. cryptocurrency exchange and custodian. It allows Coinbase to shift from a patchwork of state licenses to a single federal framework, with plans to expand digital asset custody, stablecoin services, and payments offerings. What the Approval Means for Coinbase Rick Schonberg, Coinbase’s head of prime trading and custody , described the approval as the result of years of advocacy for clearer rules and stronger oversight. “The OCC’s approval allows us to expand our custody capabilities within a consistent federal regulatory framework,” Schonberg said in a company statement. “As digital assets become more connected to the financial system, clear and consistent oversight matters. This approval is a step toward aligning digital-asset custody with the infrastructure that individuals and institutions know and rely on.” Coinbase has operated under state-level crypto licenses for nearly a decade, including New York’s BitLicense and a limited-purpose trust charter. Company representatives noted that a federal framework has become increasingly important as the digital assets industry matures and integrates more deeply with traditional finance. Under the national trust charter, Coinbase gains two primary advantages: Federal preemption of certain state financial laws that apply to OCC-regulated entities. Operation under the OCC’s recently finalized federal supervisory framework for these charters. The company’s near-term priorities include strengthening digital asset custody and eventually expanding into stablecoin issuance, servicing, white-label stablecoin arrangements for other firms, and payments. Part of a Broader Wave of Crypto Charters Coinbase’s final approval is the latest in a series of national trust bank charters granted or conditionally approved during the second Trump administration. The OCC has processed nearly two dozen such charters in this period, with more than a dozen going to cryptocurrency firms and a similar number to fintech companies. Coinbase was among the first five crypto firms to receive conditional approval from the OCC in December 2025. Late last month, the agency also granted final approval to Ripple’s national trust charter application. This surge reflects a more accommodative regulatory stance toward digital assets at the federal level compared with previous administrations. Ongoing Legal Challenge from Traditional Banks The wave of trust charter approvals has not gone unchallenged. Traditional banking groups have filed a lawsuit against the OCC, arguing that the agency’s interpretation of national trust bank charters improperly allows crypto companies to operate with bank-like powers while avoiding full banking regulations and federal deposit insurance protections. Assets held in these national trust banks are not covered by FDIC insurance, a key distinction from traditional banks. Critics contend this creates an uneven playing field and potential risks for consumers. The litigation and any subsequent appeals could take years to resolve. Courts will ultimately decide whether the OCC’s interpretation of the relevant statutes is lawful and what remedies, if any, should apply to institutions already chartered under the current framework. Possible outcomes include tighter restrictions on existing charters or a broader reversal of the OCC’s approach. Looking Ahead For Coinbase, the final OCC approval provides greater regulatory certainty and a clearer path to scale custody and payments infrastructure under federal supervision. Industry observers will watch how quickly the company rolls out expanded stablecoin and payments services, and whether other major crypto firms accelerate their own federal charter applications. The decision also underscores the evolving relationship between digital asset companies and the traditional banking system. While the national trust charter model offers a pathway for crypto firms to operate under federal oversight, the unresolved legal challenges mean the long-term contours of this regulatory approach remain unsettled. As Coinbase begins operating under its new federal charter, the company positions itself as one of the most prominent examples of crypto firms integrating more formally into the U.S. financial regulatory architecture.

Whale wallets are growing, exchange supply is falling, and his trading indicator has issued a buy alert. Hilton argues these signals are arriving simultaneously and confirm that large holders are buying XRP at current prices. That figure represents 28 new wallets in just 10 days. Hilton describes this as “major accumulation signal” territory. Large holders, in his view, represent “the smart money in the room.” These wallets have added over 60 million XRP in the last two weeks alone. XRP holders! It is happening right now, and it is happening right in front of all of us! pic.twitter.com/8PeWAEiJDr — Austin Hilton (@austinahilton) November 8, 2026 XRP is Leaving Exchanges Exchange supply is also declining . He noted that XRP holdings on major platforms like Binance, Coinbase, and Crypto.com have dropped by 149 million, bringing exchange supply to 22.34 billion. Hilton says this is a signal many people misread. When XRP leaves exchanges and moves into private wallets or cold storage, holders are signaling they do not plan to sell. Exchanges are where most XRP gets sold. Removing the asset from that environment suggests long-term conviction. A Trading Indicator Confirms the Zone Hilton also referenced his proprietary trading indicator, which has generated a buy alert for XRP. He walked through previous signals, noting gains of 44%, 13%, and 48% across prior buy-to-sell cycles. XRP is currently trading at $1.15, below its 200-day moving average. His indicator is showing the same accumulation signal currently visible in XLM, which recently produced a 39% move following three consecutive buy signals. Key Levels and Liquidity Hilton says XRP can recover above $1.30 to $1.40 in the near term, but only if liquidity returns to the crypto market. He sees current conditions as bearish, with money flowing into short positions on XRP, Bitcoin, and Ethereum. Inflation data and Federal Reserve decisions will play a role in determining when that liquidity shifts. He also flagged macro risks including geopolitical tensions as potential headwinds. What to Watch Hilton outlined three metrics to track. He wants to see whether million-XRP wallets continue to grow, whether large holders keep adding to their positions , and whether exchange balances continue to decline. He acknowledged XRP could still see further downside if the broader market pulls back. Despite that, he says the accumulation data is clear. “Accumulation signals are everywhere,” he stated. The next catalyst is a liquidity event that returns buying pressure to the market. Disclaimer : This content is meant to inform and should not be considered financial advice. Data.title: Stellar Foundation Backs Marketnode to Expand Tokenized Funds Across Asia-Pacific
Data.body: TL;DR: The Stellar Development Foundation announced a strategic investment in Marketnode on October 29, aiming to widen institutional access to tokenized investment products in Asia-Pacific. Marketnode is backed by Euroclear, HSBC, SGX Group and Temasek, but the announcement did not disclose an investment amount or ownership percentage. Tokenization is frequently described as a technology that makes financial assets available on a blockchain. The harder part is often distribution: who is allowed to buy the product, how ownership is recorded, and which regulated institutions can service it. That is the focus of a Stellar Development Foundation investment announced October 29 . The foundation said it had made a strategic investment in Marketnode, an Asia-Pacific digital-market-infrastructure company with backing from Euroclear, HSBC, SGX Group and Temasek. Infrastructure for products, not just tokens Marketnode works with funds, credit products and structured investments, supplying technology and services for issuance, distribution and ongoing servicing. The ambition is to connect the firms that originate investment products with distributors and eligible investors using blockchain rails where appropriate. A token representing a fund interest does not necessarily make that fund available to anyone with a wallet. Eligibility requirements, investor onboarding, local laws, transfer restrictions and redemption arrangements still apply. In institutional markets, making those controls work is often the difference between an experiment and a product that can be distributed at scale. The announcement says Marketnode has already worked with global and regional asset managers and has discussed onchain access to select BNY Investments funds on Stellar. It also identifies relationships with asset managers including Franklin Templeton, Maybank Asset Management, CGS International and WisdomTree. Those references are evidence of an existing institutional network, but they should not be read as a guarantee that every product from every named organisation is universally available or that all its assets have migrated to Stellar. Why Asia-Pacific is a strategic market The region contains large financial centres, significant cross-border investment activity and a range of approaches to regulated digital assets. A platform that can coordinate issuance and distribution may lower some operational friction between asset managers, custodians and investors. Still, a public blockchain can supply only part of the solution. Legal title, disclosure, investor protections, tax reporting and reconciliation with traditional securities systems remain essential. Marketnode’s experience with institutional processes may be as important to the foundation’s plans as the underlying Stellar network itself. For comparison, NewsBTC has covered the NYSE’s plans for tokenized-securities infrastructure . Tokenization and settlement are related pieces of a wider market-infrastructure problem, and both must fit the compliance standards that institutions already face. What the investment does not reveal Neither the monetary value of the investment nor the stake acquired was specified in the foundation’s announcement. That limits any attempt to infer Marketnode’s valuation or measure how much capital Stellar is committing relative to its other ecosystem investments. There is also a difference between financial backing and market adoption. An investment can help a company build integrations, expand teams or develop products, but proof of use will come from assets actually issued, transactions settled, and institutions actively servicing customers over time. The next useful milestones would include disclosed product launches, participating financial institutions, client access arrangements and measurable volume. Stellar has identified a credible institutional distribution problem and is backing a company that works on it. How much of that infrastructure eventually runs through its network remains the question to watch. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae. Data.title: Blockchain.com Appoints Lisa Nelson and Luis Berruga to Board of Directors
Data.body: BitcoinWorld Media Blockchain.com Appoints Lisa Nelson and Luis Berruga to Board of Directors New appointments bolster board experience in scaling finance and technology growth companies LONDON , Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Blockchain.com , a global leader in crypto services for retail and institutional users, today announced the appointments of former Microsoft executive, Lisa Nelson, and former Global X ETFs CEO, Luis Berruga, to its board of directors. Nelson and Berruga’s appointments add further diversity of background and expertise in scaling technology, traditional finance and digital assets growth companies to Blockchain.com’s board. With respective experience operating or serving on the boards of publicly traded companies like Microsoft and SOL Strategies, Nelson and Berruga strengthen the board’s expertise in corporate governance, financial oversight, strategic growth and emerging technologies. “The exceptional caliber and strength of our board already stands out in the digital assets industry and reflects the ambition of Blockchain.com,” said Peter Smith, Executive Chairman, CEO, and Co-Founder of Blockchain.com. “Lisa and Luis bring complementary experience across global finance, technology and scaling growth companies. Their diverse perspectives will be invaluable as we continue to scale our own business.” “Digital assets are moving from the margins of finance toward its core, and that shift will reward companies that earn trust at scale. Blockchain.com has done that for 15 years, across every market cycle,” said Lisa Nelson, Board Director of Blockchain.com. “I’m honored to join the board and help guide its next chapter, building on that foundation with rigor and a relentless focus on customers seeking modern solutions to archaic, legacy financial services.” “Sitting at the intersection of traditional finance and decentralized finance for much of my recent work, it’s clear that more assets of all types are going to move onchain,” said Luis Berruga, Board Director of Blockchain.com. “Blockchain.com is perfectly positioned to help connect traditional financial markets with the growing onchain economy. I’m very much looking forward to helping scale the business alongside the rest of the board and management team.” Nelson currently serves on the boards of Banqer Software, Spark New Zealand and Brooks Running. She also advises several venture funds and early-stage tech startups around the world. Nelson is an almost 15-year veteran of Microsoft, where she held executive positions in finance, investor relations, and business development. She also co-founded Microsoft’s first venture fund, M12, and as its managing director, helped deploy hundreds of millions of dollars in funding across more than 80 startups globally. Nelson is a CPA and began her career at EY. Berruga also serves as an independent director of SOL Strategies, lead independent trustee and audit committee chairman of the Tidal ETF platform, an independent trustee of KraneShares ETFs, and an independent director of the VistaOne Fund by Vista Equity Partners. He was also CEO and board chair of Global X ETFs, which he scaled from a startup into a leading ETF platform, with assets under management of $85 billion across more than 150 ETFs on four continents. Earlier in his career, Berruga spent time at Jefferies and Morgan Stanley. About Blockchain.com: Blockchain.com is connecting the world to the future of finance. The most trusted and fastest-growing global crypto company helps millions safely access cryptocurrency. Since its inception in 2011, Blockchain.com has supported over 95M+ wallets, 44M+ confirmed accounts, and more than $1.1 trillion in crypto transactions. Operating in more than 70 jurisdictions, Blockchain.com offers secure self-custody, institutional services, and a growing product suite aligned with global regulation and privacy standards.
